aspects.says: A worker blocked in an ordinary wait is lost to the pool, so waiters can hold every worker while the task that would release them sits in the queue; managedBlock lets the pool add a spare worker.
basis: section:A Worker That Blocks Is Lost to the Pool, Unless It Blocks Through managedBlock()

aspects.says: A pool you create keeps its workers after its last task until you close or shut it down, also when the work throws; idle workers end only slowly.
basis: section:A Pool You Create Keeps Its Threads Until You Close It

aspects.says: A ForkJoinTask handed to execute() that fails leaves its exception in the task, where nobody sees it unless the task is kept and joined.
basis: section:A Failure Reaches the Caller Through invoke() or join(), and execute() Keeps It in the Task

aspects.says: fork() called from a thread that is no pool's worker schedules the task in the common pool, not in a pool you created.
basis: section:invoke() Waits for One Task; submit() Lets Them All Run

aspects.says: Some JDK waits (Condition.await, the blocking queues tried, CompletableFuture.join) already block through managedBlock; CountDownLatch, Semaphore, sleep, Object.wait and socket reads do not.
basis: section:A Worker That Blocks Is Lost to the Pool, Unless It Blocks Through managedBlock()

aspects.says: invoke() waits for one task, so tasks handed over one invoke at a time never run together; submitting all before joining any runs them together.
basis: section:invoke() Waits for One Task; submit() Lets Them All Run

aspects.says: A pool per request without close() makes the thread count climb under steady traffic, since workers outlive the request and are daemon threads only in that they don't keep the JVM alive.
basis: section:A Pool You Create Keeps Its Threads Until You Close It

aspects.says: invoke() and join() rethrow a task's unchecked exception as its own type, get() wraps it in an ExecutionException, and after execute() the exception stays in the task.
basis: section:A Failure Reaches the Caller Through invoke() or join(), and execute() Keeps It in the Task
